title: Delete the herd execution packages and their tk commands
description:
Delete the herd execution packages and the `tk herd` commands that drive them.
ticfac owns this now.

GOES — `internal/herd/`:
  client, herdtest, gitcmd, spawn, wait, reconcile, cleanup, state, notify,
  paint, collect.

STAYS — and this is the whole judgement in this tick:
  - `relay` — the durable operator question. Tracker domain, wired into
    operator.Engine across ~15 call sites. It is not execution.
  - `dashboard` — it exists to JOIN tracker state with run state; WaveRow and
    TickRow are built from tick.Tick and state.Manifest in one function, so
    there is no seam inside the type. It becomes a CONSUMER of ticfac rather
    than a part of it.

  Both currently depend on packages in the GOES list — dashboard on `state`,
  relay via the herd_wait command. Decide how they survive: dashboard needs a
  supported way to read run state (ticfac's `.ticfac/` records, or its run
  feed), and relay needs whatever herd_wait gave it. That decision is this
  tick's real work; the deletions are the easy half.

ALSO GOES — `cmd/tk/cmd/`:
  herd_spawn, herd_collect, herd_cleanup, herd_reconcile, herd_watch,
  herd_notify, herd_paint, herd_wait, herd_plugin, herd_shared and their tests,
  minus whatever `relay` and `dashboard` still need.

DO NOT TOUCH: `internal/tkcontract` — cmd/tk's own version and root contract
gate use it.

Also close the ten direct `.tick/` reads the retired packages hold (state.go's
RelDir and Write/Read/List, config's FileName and LoadRepo, paint's tick.NewStore,
dashboard's snapshot and fswatch, collect's boundary diff). Each either goes with
its package or becomes a callback on something that stays.

Sequence: land azq first. Then delete in an order where `go build ./...` passes
after every commit — a broken intermediate state on an irreversible change is
how a deletion becomes a rewrite.
